Explain intermittent test timeouts in CI
The integration suite in C:/work/payments-core takes 14 minutes in CI and times out about one run in ten at the 20 minute job limit. Locally the suite runs in 6 minutes. The suite uses pytest with pytest-xdist set to -n 4 in CI and -n 8 locally, and it uses a Postgres service container configured in .github/workflows/integration.yml. The slowest tests are listed in reports/durations_ci.txt, and the conftest files are at tests/integration/conftest.py and tests/conftest.py.

Task: find the cause of both the slowdown and the timeouts, and say which one is the root cause. Start with reports/durations_ci.txt and sort the tests by total duration, then group them by fixture or module. Read tests/integration/conftest.py and check for session-scoped fixtures that create a fresh database per test module, and check whether they run migrations each time. Read tests/conftest.py for an autouse fixture that calls time.sleep or that waits for a port.

Check the Postgres service container in the workflow file. Look at the health check options, the shared memory size and the max_connections setting. With -n 4 workers and a connection pool of 10 per worker, check whether the pool can exhaust max_connections. Check whether the tests share a database name across workers, which would cause one worker to drop a database another worker uses, and whether the database name includes the xdist worker id.

Check the timeout failures in the CI logs under logs/ci_timeout_run_4471.txt. Look for the last test that started before the cancellation and whether it is a test that waits on a lock or a queue.

Constraints: do not modify tests or configuration. Do not trigger a CI run. You may read the logs and the configuration files only. Do not print any connection string with a password; mask it.

Report back: a ranked list of at most three causes with file and line for each, the duration table grouped by module for the top five modules, the explanation of why the timeout is intermittent, and the one config change to test first. Keep the report under 40 lines.

Add retry budget to HTTP client
Context: the Python service at clients/partner_api/ calls a partner REST API. When the partner has an incident, every worker retries each failed request up to five times with exponential backoff, which multiplies traffic by six and makes the outage worse. We need a retry budget: a client may only retry when retries make up less than 10 percent of recent requests over a sliding 60-second window.

Requirements: add a class RetryBudget in clients/partner_api/budget.py. It has a method allow_retry() returning True or False, and a method record_request() that the client calls on every first attempt. Keep counts in a deque of timestamps, using time.monotonic. Use a lock from threading so the class is safe across threads. The budget must allow a minimum of 10 retries per window, even when traffic is very low, so that a single failure at low volume can still be retried. Pass an injectable clock function in the constructor, defaulting to time.monotonic, so tests can control time.

Integration: in clients/partner_api/client.py, the request method must call budget.allow_retry() before each retry. If it returns False, raise PartnerRetryBudgetExhausted, a new exception class defined in clients/partner_api/errors.py, and keep the original exception as its __cause__. The client's existing retry count of five remains the upper limit.

Constraints: do not add a dependency. Do not change the public signature of the request method. Do not change the backoff timing function in clients/partner_api/backoff.py. Keep the new code under 120 lines in total.

Tests: add clients/partner_api/tests/test_budget.py. Use the injected clock to test the minimum-of-ten rule, the ten percent ratio, the window expiry after 60 seconds, and a concurrent call test with ten threads. Add one client test that makes the budget exhausted and checks that the exception is raised with its cause.

Verification: run pytest clients/partner_api -q and paste the summary. Run ruff check clients/partner_api and paste the output. Run pytest clients/partner_api/tests/test_budget.py -q -p no:randomly and paste the output.

Report back: the files you added or changed, the numbers you chose and why, the test results, and any open question about the ten-retry minimum that the team should decide. Keep it under 30 lines.

Add health detail for Postgres replicas
Context: the FastAPI service at services/status has a health endpoint in services/status/routers/health.py that returns only overall status. The on-call team wants a detailed endpoint that reports the lag of each Postgres read replica, so they can see replication delay without logging into the database. The replica list comes from the environment variable REPLICA_DSNS, which holds a comma-separated list of connection strings. The lag is read with the query SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()). The database helper already exists in services/status/db/pool.py as a function get_connection(dsn).

Requirements: add a new route GET /health/replicas in routers/health.py. The response is a JSON list where each element has dsn_host, lag_seconds as a float, and status set to ok when lag is under 30 seconds, otherwise lagging. If a replica cannot be reached within two seconds, return an element with status unreachable and lag_seconds null. Never include the password part of the DSN in the response. Parse the host with urllib.parse.urlsplit and return only the hostname.

Constraints: do not change the existing /health route. Do not add a new dependency. Do not cache results. Do not query the primary database. Use the existing dependency injection pattern used in routers/health.py. Add a short comment only where the two-second timeout is set, explaining why.

Tests: add tests in services/status/tests/test_health_replicas.py. Use a fake connection factory passed through the same dependency override the router already uses, so no real database is needed. Cover ok, lagging, unreachable and an empty REPLICA_DSNS value. Also assert that the password does not appear in the response body for a DSN that contains a password.

Verification: run pytest services/status/tests/test_health_replicas.py -q and paste the summary. Run pytest services/status -q and paste the summary. Run ruff check services/status and paste the output.

Report back: the files you added or changed, the route signature, the test names, the three command outputs, and any decision you made about empty REPLICA_DSNS. Keep the report under 30 lines.

Requirements: the queue client is in worker/queue/client.py and has a property is_connected that returns a bool and a method ping() that returns a float latency in seconds, raising QueueUnavailable when the connection is down. In worker/http/ready.py, call ping() with a timeout of 0.5 seconds, using the existing helper with_timeout in worker/util/timeouts.py. Return HTTP 200 with body {"ready": true, "queue_latency_ms": <int>} when ping succeeds. Return HTTP 503 with body {"ready": false, "reason": "queue unavailable"} when ping raises QueueUnavailable or the timeout expires.

Constraints: the liveness endpoint GET /live must not change, and it must not call the queue. Do not cache ping results. Do not log every probe; log only on state change, meaning when readiness flips from ready to not ready or back, using a module-level variable named last_ready. Keep the change inside worker/http/ready.py and worker/queue/client.py if ping does not exist yet; if it exists, do not modify client.py.
